text: [3:549] Compare—no insurance coverage for 50% penalty for “serious and willful misconduct”: A compensation award may be increased by 50% where the employee's injuries result from “serious and willful misconduct” by the employer. [Lab.C. § 4553] Insurers may not indemnify the employer against this liability: “An insurer shall not insure against the liability of the employer for the additional compensation recoverable for serious and willful misconduct of the employer or his agent.” [Ins.C. § 11661; see Azevedo v. Abel (1968) 264 CA2d 451, 457, 70 CR 710, 714, fn. 10; see also Imperial Irrigation Dist. v. Chubb/Pacific Indem. Group (1979) 95 CA3d 317, 320-321, 157 CR 733, 734—applies to any CGL insurer entering the field of workers' compensation indemnity] (1) [3:550] Duty to defend against charges of “serious and willful misconduct”? The ban on indemnifying against the penalty does not prevent an insurer from covering the cost of defending against charges of “serious and willful misconduct.” [Ins.C. § 11661] But not every workers' compensation policy does so.
